question: GQ-001
subject: the rights filter rejected 86% of a want-list, and it was right to
the_trigger: the eighth want-list yielded only 476 eligible of 3,409 — a 14% pass rate against 51% on the seventh. 2,933 books excluded is worth understanding before accepting.

my_hypothesis_was_wrong.what_i_expected: bare-assertion would hold old books whose age makes them unambiguously public domain regardless of metadata wording — a filter too literal to notice
my_hypothesis_was_wrong.what_i_measured: of 2,761 bare-assertion items only FIFTEEN were published before 1900, and 42 before 1929
my_hypothesis_was_wrong.what_they_actually_are: 1950s-2000s material — 595 from the 2000s, 728 from the 1990s, 526 from the 1970s

why_the_pass_rate_fell.seventh_list_subjects: Zoology, Medicine, Agriculture, Astronomy — 96 items from the 2000s
why_the_pass_rate_fell.eighth_list_subjects: Physics, Mathematics, Engineering, Philosophy — 595 from the 2000s
why_the_pass_rate_fell.conclusion: six times as much modern material. The pass rate tracks the subject era, not a change in the filter.

verdict: NO CHANGE. A plain "Public Domain" string on a 1994 engineering text is exactly the unverified assertion this filter exists to catch. The 14% is the filter working.
what_would_change_my_mind: a bare-assertion bucket dominated by pre-1929 material, where age settles the question independently of metadata wording
